source.title: Transformers converge to invariant algorithmic cores

record.tranche_reason: The study trains transformers on modular addition and measures delayed generalization, but uses ACE and a distinct mechanistic analysis rather than reproducing the original measurement procedure.
record.gate_note: Included the modular-addition training and scaling results, the weight-decay comparison, and Markov-chain results relevant to whether same-task runs implement the same algorithm. The subject–verb agreement and open-ended generation results are not grokking tests. Layer-selection results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains transformers on modular addition, shows delayed generalization, and measures delay versus modulus and weight decay. It tracks core dimension, operator fit and rotational modes across training and compares modes across seeds. Its method (ACE cores, operator spectra) differs from the originals' Fourier/progress-measure analysis, so T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but conflates two results. The authors conclude that cores crystallize at grokking with cyclic operators that differ in modes across seeds. Functional redundancy (more equivalent modes, larger p) accelerates the memorization-to-generalization transition, giving τ ∝ 1/(ωp) with a critical pcrit. Separately, continued weight decay after grokking inflates cores across redundant modes. Broader claim: transformers converge to invariant low-dimensional cores, including in Markov and LLM settings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses transformers trained on modular addition and tracks training and test accuracy, but adds ACE-based core extraction and operator analysis. The specified modular-addition experiment uses mod 53, an even train/test split, and AdamW; the scaling sweep varies p and uses one-layer transformers.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported grokking delay varies with weight decay and modulus; post-grokking core size and mode counts differ depending on whether weight decay is maintained or disabled.

fits_no_version.finding: Three Markov-chain transformers with near-orthogonal core subspaces recover the same transition spectrum to within a few percent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained transformers on a non-grokking stochastic task converge to the same algorithm up to change of coordinates.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026
record.problems: The modular-addition grokking experiment uses three models. Scaling results are reported as aggregate fits, with individual plotted delays not stated in the text. The paper reports that the grokking delay diverges near fitted pcrit, but the empirical modulus sweep begins at p = 31 while p̂crit ≈ 23.

untested.parts: Only modular addition. Training fraction is never varied independently of p.
Removal of memorizing components is not measured. No explicit progress measure is evaluated for anticipating the jump; only coarse checkpoints exist.
Entire version: no non-algorithmic grokking and no initialization-scale manipulation.
Entire version: the LLM experiments study subject–verb agreement cores, not delayed generalization.
No sizes below the fitted pcrit, no ungrokking, and no direct memorizing-versus-generalizing circuit norm comparison.
No architecture or hyperparameter variation; three seeds only.
Entire version: only AdamW used, no optimizer or numerical-precision controls.

missing.what: Pre-grokking checkpoint values that show continuous progress before the test jump: epoch 0 (acc 0.01, Rh2 -0.58, core dim 42) and epoch 300 (acc 0.04, Rh2 0.38, core dim 33).
Number of rotational modes at grokking exceeds the single minimally required mode in each seed.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V2 'challenges' label is not supported: the paper's own checkpoint values show progress before the jump, and its theory describes a smooth margin trajectory. R11 was reclassified from reversed to partial because the algorithm class is shared. Markov rows were delinked because that task involves no grokking.

versions.untested_parts: The modular-addition experiment uses one modulus and the scaling sweep uses the stated prime moduli; it does not test other algorithmic datasets.
The study does not test whether memorizing components are removed later, or whether a continuous progress measure anticipates the test-accuracy jump.
The empirical modulus sweep does not include values below the fitted pcrit; the study does not directly compare the proposed circuit with a separately measured memorizing circuit.
The same-task comparisons use independent seeds in the Markov and modular-addition experiments, not a broad architecture or hyperparameter sweep.

rows.subject: three two-layer transformers (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition and track training and test accuracy.

conditions.value: all 532 = 2809 input pairs, split evenly into train and test sets

rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over training; grokking timing
rows.value: Test accuracy remained near chance until spiking around epoch 800; the grokking epoch was the first analysis time point at which all three models achieved perfect test accuracy, at epoch 800. The text describes high training accuracy preceding delayed test accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: mean±sem shown; numerical uncertainty not stated
rows.note: Aggregate result for the three models. The appendix says grokking was defined by all three reaching perfect test accuracy; it does not give an exact epoch for training-accuracy saturation.
rows.check: Condition 'training: 2 × 10^3 epochs' covers the grokking phase only. Appendix C says models were trained 2×10^4 epochs with AdamW lr 1e-3, batch 512. No memorization (train-saturation) epoch is given, so the size of the delay is read only from test accuracy staying near chance until about epoch 800.

source_check.correct: Section 4 describes the initial 2×10^3 epochs; Appendix C specifies 2×10^4 total epochs, AdamW learning rate 10^-3, batch size 512 and weight decay 1. All three models first achieved perfect test accuracy at the epoch-800 analysis checkpoint.
source_check.problem: The stated training duration covers the initial analysis window rather than the complete training run.

rows.subject: one-layer transformers (aggregate over 12 random seeds per condition)
rows.operation_detail: Sweep prime modulus p while holding weight decay at ω = 1; measure grokking delay.

conditions.value: p2 input pairs randomly partitioned into a 50/50 train/test split

rows.measure: Grokking delay τgrok = τgen − τmem as a function of p
rows.value: Grokking time scales inversely with redundancy p; the ODE fit has R2 > 0.99 and fitted p̂crit ≈ 23. The text says the delay diverges near pcrit.
rows.note: The paper treats p as functional redundancy; because the dataset contains p2 pairs with a 50/50 split, increasing p also increases training-set size. Individual plotted delays are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Training fraction is fixed at 50%. Smaller training sets come only from smaller p, which also changes the number of classes, so for V1 dataset size is confounded with task size. For V5, pcrit ≈ 23 is an extrapolated ODE fit parameter: the sweep starts at p = 31, and no point at or below pcrit or any ungrokking is shown. Optimizer is full-batch AdamW.

source_check.correct: Observed for V1's delay association within this modulus sweep; cannot_determine for V5's efficiency competition and critical training-dataset size. The fitted threshold is a critical modulus, approximately 23, extrapolated from measurements at p≥31.
source_check.problem: The observed state overextends the modulus-scaling result to V5; task size, class count and training-set size change together.

rows.subject: one-layer transformers (aggregate over 12 random seeds per condition)
rows.operation_detail: Sweep weight decay while holding p = 53; measure grokking delay.
rows.measure: Grokking delay τgrok as a function of weight decay
rows.value: Observed fit τ ∝ ω−1.02, matching the stated theoretical prediction ω−1.
rows.note: Aggregate scaling fit; individual plotted delays are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Bears on V5 only as weight decay setting the grokking timescale (τ ∝ ω^-1.02). It does not measure circuit efficiency or the memorization–generalization competition.

source_check.correct: State for V5: cannot_determine. The measured result is grokking-delay scaling τ∝ω^-1.02, consistent with the paper's ω^-1 timescale prediction.
source_check.problem: A weight-decay timescale does not measure preference for an efficient generalizing circuit over memorization.

rows.subject: three two-layer modular-addition transformers (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Continue training with weight decay maintained or disable it after branching at epoch 900; track core dimension.

conditions.value: maintained at ω = 1 versus disabled (ω → 0) after epoch 900

rows.measure: Extracted core dimension over continued training
rows.baseline: Core dimension at grokking was approximately 13–14
rows.value: With weight decay maintained, cores progressively inflated from approximately 15 to 60 dimensions; disabling weight decay post-grokking kept cores more compact.
rows.uncertainty: mean±sem shown; numerical uncertainty not stated
rows.note: The paper describes inflation under continued weight decay, rather than a progressively simplifying or compacting generalizing circuit.
rows.check: Remove the V2 link: post-grokking inflation of the generalizing core is not removal of memorizing components. For V5, maintained weight decay makes the generalizing solution more redundant (core about 15→60 dims), not more compact. 'Efficient' holds only in the minimum-norm sense.

source_check.correct: State for V5: cannot_determine. Continued decay expands extracted cores from approximately 15 to 60 dimensions; disabling decay at epoch 900 preserves more compact cores.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4, core-inflation paragraph; Figure 3A; Appendix C
source_check.problem: Post-grokking core size does not establish incomplete norm efficiency or competition with memorization.

rows.subject: three two-layer modular-addition transformers (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compare necessary and sufficient core dimensions over continued training with weight decay maintained.
rows.measure: Dimensions sufficient to preserve baseline accuracy and necessary to prevent chance-level performance
rows.value: Sufficient dimension remained stable, while necessary dimension expanded dramatically; the paper attributes the difference to increasing redundancy.
rows.uncertainty: mean±sem shown; numerical uncertainty not stated
rows.note: This result indicates redundancy growth under continued weight decay, not a measured preference for a smaller generalizing circuit.
rows.check: Measures sufficient versus necessary core dimensions after grokking, i.e. redundancy growth. No norm is measured and there is no memorization comparison.

source_check.correct: State for V5: cannot_determine. Sufficient dimension remains stable while the number of dimensions whose removal reduces performance to chance increases.
source_check.problem: Redundancy growth after generalization does not measure the efficiency-account effect named in V5.

rows.subject: three two-layer modular-addition transformers (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Track rotational modes in fitted core operators with weight decay maintained or disabled after epoch 900.

conditions.value: maintained at ω = 1 versus disabled (ω → 0) after epoch 900

rows.measure: Number of rotational modes in the fitted core operator
rows.baseline: One mode minimally required, as stated in the text
rows.value: With weight decay maintained, mode counts approached the theoretical maximum ⌊p/2⌋ = 26 by the terminal epoch; disabling weight decay kept mode counts sparse and stable.
rows.uncertainty: mean±sem shown; numerical uncertainty not stated
rows.note: The reported result is increasing redundant modes, rather than evidence that weight decay produces a uniquely minimal circuit.
rows.check: Mode counts approach 26 under maintained weight decay versus sparse modes without it. Weight decay distributes the generalizing computation rather than selecting a minimal circuit.

source_check.correct: State for V5: cannot_determine. Maintained decay drives rotational-mode counts toward 26; disabling decay preserves sparse mode counts. The paper's minimum-norm argument explicitly permits maximum redundancy.
source_check.problem: More rotational modes do not contradict greater norm efficiency.

rows.subject: three two-layer modular-addition transformers (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: trained through grokking; checkpoints analyzed every 100 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Extract cores over training and fit linear operators to second-layer shift dynamics in core coordinates.
rows.measure: Core formation and fitted-operator eigenvalue locations
rows.baseline: Before grokking, fitted eigenvalues were scattered inside the unit circle
rows.value: Cores crystallized coincident with delayed generalization; at grokking, operator eigenvalues snapped onto the unit circle.
rows.note: The reported timing is coincident with grokking, rather than a stated gradual circuit-formation measure that anticipates the accuracy jump.
rows.check: Fig. 2C shows continuous measures already moving before the jump. At epoch 300 (test acc 0.04), core dim fell from 42 to 33 and Rh2 rose from -0.58 to 0.38. Unit-circle eigenvalues appear only at the epoch-800 checkpoint. With 100-epoch checkpoints, 'coincident' does not rule out anticipation, so not a challenge.

rows.subject: three two-layer modular-addition transformers (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compare cyclic operator modes recovered from each independently trained model.
rows.measure: Identity of rotational modes in fitted core operators
rows.value: All three models converged to cyclic operators, but the specific rotational modes differed across runs.
rows.note: The text states that the task permits multiple valid modes and that models need not agree on which modes, or how many, to use.
rows.check: Not reversed. All three seeds converge to the same algorithm class (cyclic rotational operators) but use different rotational modes/frequencies. This is the same algorithm with different key frequencies, not different algorithms.

source_check.correct: State for V6: observed. All three models recover cyclic rotational operators; selected modes and multiplicities differ within that algorithmic family.
source_check.problem: Different frequencies and multiplicities do not establish different algorithms under V6's wording.

tranche.reason: The study measures delayed generalization and investigates its mechanism with ACE extraction, causal ablations, operator analysis and scaling sweeps.

source_check.notes: Several pack values are truncated; checks cover their visible assertions. R7 is cited but not listed for checking, so its associated verdicts were checked directly against Figure 2C.

statements.correction: Maintained post-grokking decay: extracted core dimensions approximately 15→60; rotational modes approach 26. Disabled decay: compact cores and sparse modes. Proposed explanation: minimum norm distributes computation across redundant modes.
statements.problem: The reported expansion and mode counts are correct, but treating them as a limitation of V5 equates norm efficiency with compactness. The experiment occurs after grokking and does not compare generalizing and memorizing solutions.

statements.correction: Three modular-addition seeds: cyclic operators in every model; different rotational modes and multiplicities; shared algorithmic family with variable implementations.
statements.problem: Mode and multiplicity differences are correctly reported, but their placement as evidence against V6 overstates what varies: all three models recover cyclic rotational computation.
